behavSSF

Fit hidden Markov step-selection models for animal movement. The package lets you check how starting values affect the fitted states, give those states names using your own rules, and compare simulated tracks with the GPS data.

This is a development preview. Source code · Download the source package

Start with a worked example

  • Hwange zebra. Apply the published rules to a GPS track and see which steps are labelled travelling, foraging or resting.
  • Red deer. Find the steps that change labels between two fitted solutions and see how that changes the share ending in forest.
  • Andean condor. Define a taxonomy for flight states and compare the fitted labels with a proxy from the GPS track.
  • African elephant. See how lagged step lengths change the daily peak in step-length correlation.

Install from GitHub 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("AurelienNicosiaULaval/behavSSF")
library(behavSSF)

Installation requires a C++ toolchain. The reference workflow introduces the published rules and the functions that implement them.

Credits

Ilhem Bouderbala wrote the original research functions. Aurélien Nicosia reworked them for the R package and added plots, ways to present fitted results, and support for new state taxonomies. The published method is by Ilhem Bouderbala, Aurélien Nicosia and Daniel Fortin. Article in PLOS ONE
